strategy_title: TMA Block Pointers Worsen Bank Conflicts in Fused Kernel
strategy_description: Replacing scalar pointer arithmetic with tl.make_block_ptr + tl.advance in a fused Triton kernel caused a 38% regression (146 us → 238 us). Despite reducing registers/thread from 168 to 128 and improving theoretical occupancy from 18.75% to 25%, the shared memory bank conflicts worsened significantly: average conflict way increased from 7.9 to 11.9, excessive wavefronts rose from 66% to 75%, and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction more than doubled from 7.05 to 15.01 cycles. The block pointer approach did not eliminate the underlying non-contiguous access pattern causing bank conflicts — instead it increased the total shared memory wavefront count (22.9M → 41.0M), suggesting the TMA staging introduced additional shared memory traffic rather than bypassing it.
slow_pseudocode:
# Manual scalar pointer arithmetic (baseline)
offs_k = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    xindex = offs_k[None,:] + k_idx*BLOCK_K + 192*offs_a_m[:,None]
    a = tl.load(A + xindex, eviction_policy='evict_first')
    b = tl.load(B + tl.broadcast_to(b_k_idx + 192*offs_b_n[None,:], [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]))
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# TMA block pointer style (regressed)
a_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(A, shape=(M,K), strides=(stride_am,stride_ak),
    offsets=(pid_m*BLOCK_M, 0), block_shape=(BLOCK_M,BLOCK_K), order=(1,0))
b_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(B, shape=(K,N), strides=(stride_bk,stride_bn),
    offsets=(0, pid_n*BLOCK_N), block_shape=(BLOCK_K,BLOCK_N), order=(0,1))
for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(a_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    b = tl.load(b_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False, out_dtype=tl.float32)
    a_block_ptr = tl.advance(a_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
    b_block_ptr = tl.advance(b_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
applicable_when: Never — this specific transformation made things worse. Do not apply tl.make_block_ptr as a bank-conflict fix in this kernel.
do_not_apply_when: When the kernel already has severe shared memory bank conflicts (SharedMemoryConflicts NCU rule, >60% excessive wavefronts): switching from scalar pointer arithmetic to tl.make_block_ptr does NOT eliminate bank conflicts and can worsen them. After the change: bank conflict way increased 7.9→11.9, total shared load wavefronts increased 22.9M→41.0M, Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction doubled 7.05→15.01, and duration increased 146→238 us. The block pointer approach adds shared memory staging overhead rather than bypassing it when the access pattern is inherently non-contiguous (column-major B matrix with stride_bn=192).
framework_notes: Triton's tl.make_block_ptr on Hopper (sm_90) compiles to TMA cp.async.bulk.tensor instructions, but the staging still passes through shared memory. If the underlying access pattern causes bank conflicts (e.g., column-major matrix with large stride), TMA does not eliminate those conflicts — it may introduce additional shared memory traffic. The boundary_check=(0,1) parameter adds overhead when tensor dimensions are not multiples of block sizes.

strategy_title: Transposed B Load with tl.trans() Worsens Bank Conflicts
strategy_description: Loading the B matrix as [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] (stride-1 along K) then calling tl.trans() before tl.dot caused a 38% regression (143 us → 238 us). Despite reducing registers/thread from 168 to 128 and improving theoretical occupancy from 18.75% to 25%, shared memory bank conflicts worsened dramatically: average conflict way increased from 7.9 to 11.9, excessive wavefronts rose from 66% to 75%, and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction more than doubled from 6.93 to 15.01. The tl.trans() call does not perform a register-level transpose for free on Hopper when used as a tl.dot operand — Triton still stages the transposed tile through shared memory, and the new layout introduced worse bank conflicts than the original column-strided load. This is the same failure mode as the tl.make_block_ptr approach (item f3a7b2e9): changing the B load pattern in this fused kernel consistently worsens shared memory conflicts rather than alleviating them.
slow_pseudocode:
# Original column-strided B load (baseline, 143 us)
b_k_idx_vals = offs_k[:, None] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)  # [BLOCK_K, 1]
idx_m = b_k_idx_vals
idx_n = offs_b_n[None, :]  # [1, BLOCK_N]
xindex = idx_n + 768 * idx_m  # stride-768 between K rows
b = tl.load(B + tl.broadcast_to(idx_m + 192*idx_n, [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]))
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# Transposed B load with tl.trans() (regressed, 238 us)
b_n_idx = offs_b_n[:, None]                        # [BLOCK_N, 1]
b_k_idx = offs_k[None, :] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)     # [1, BLOCK_K]
b_xindex = b_k_idx + 192 * b_n_idx                # [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K], stride-1 along K
b_tile = tl.load(B + b_xindex, eviction_policy='evict_first')  # [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K]
b = tl.trans(b_tile)                               # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] for tl.dot
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False, out_dtype=tl.float32)
applicable_when: Never — this transformation made things worse in this kernel context.
do_not_apply_when: When a fused Triton kernel has severe shared memory bank conflicts (SharedMemoryConflicts NCU rule, >60% excessive wavefronts) caused by a column-strided B matrix load: switching to a [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] transposed load followed by tl.trans() does NOT eliminate bank conflicts. After the change: bank conflict way increased 7.9→11.9, total shared load wavefronts increased, Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction doubled 6.93→15.01, and duration increased 143→238 us. On Hopper, tl.trans() used as a tl.dot operand still routes through shared memory staging, and the transposed layout can introduce worse bank conflicts than the original. This is the third consecutive failure (TF32, tl.make_block_ptr, tl.trans) to fix bank conflicts in this kernel by changing the B load pattern.
framework_notes: On Hopper (sm_90), Triton's tl.trans() applied to a tile before tl.dot is NOT a free register-level operation — it still involves shared memory staging for the wgmma instruction. The transposed [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] layout written into shared memory can produce worse bank conflicts than the original layout depending on tile dimensions and warp access patterns. Three approaches have now failed to fix the SharedMemoryConflicts bottleneck in this kernel: (1) TF32 — correctness failure, (2) tl.make_block_ptr — 38% regression with worse conflicts, (3) tl.trans() transposed load — 38% regression with worse conflicts.

strategy_title: Increasing BLOCK_M Explodes Register Pressure, Kills Occupancy
strategy_description: Changing BLOCK_M from 64 to 128 (while keeping BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32) caused a 2x regression (145 us → 305 us). Despite the LaunchConfiguration rule predicting a 50% gain from eliminating the partial wave, registers/thread exploded from 168 to 252, collapsing theoretical occupancy from 18.75% to 12.5% and Block Limit Registers from 3 to 1 block/SM. The grid size remained 738 (unchanged from baseline) because the autotune configs did not include BLOCK_M as a tunable parameter — the constexpr BLOCK_M=128 was hardcoded but the grid lambda was not updated, so the grid did not shrink as intended. Total executed instructions nearly doubled (41.8M → 83.1M), indicating the larger tile doubled the per-block work without any grid reduction benefit.
slow_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_M=64 baseline (145 us, 168 regs/thread)
BLOCK_M : tl.constexpr = 64
BLOCK_N : tl.constexpr = 128
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 32
grid = (738, 1, 1)  # ceil(7840/64)*ceil(768/128)
acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)  # 64x128 accumulator
for k_idx in range(tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A + ...)
    b = tl.load(B + ...)
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_M=128 attempt (305 us, 252 regs/thread — REGRESSED)
BLOCK_M : tl.constexpr = 128  # doubled tile
BLOCK_N : tl.constexpr = 128
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 32
grid = (738, 1, 1)  # BUG: grid not updated, still 738 blocks
acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)  # 128x128 accumulator
for k_idx in range(tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A + ...)
    b_T = tl.load(B + ...)  # also changed B load pattern (compounding change)
    acc += tl.dot(a, tl.trans(b_T), allow_tf32=False)
applicable_when: Never in this kernel — increasing BLOCK_M when registers/thread are already at 168 (Block Limit Registers = 3) will push register count higher, not lower, because the larger accumulator tile (BLOCK_M × BLOCK_N fp32 values) dominates register usage.
do_not_apply_when: When a Triton GEMM kernel is already register-limited (Block Limit Registers ≤ 3, registers/thread ≥ 128): increasing BLOCK_M to reduce grid size will backfire. The larger accumulator tile (BLOCK_M × BLOCK_N fp32 registers) increases per-thread register count, further reducing occupancy and negating any partial-wave elimination benefit. Additionally, if the grid lambda is not updated to reflect the new BLOCK_M, the grid size remains unchanged and no partial-wave benefit is realized at all. This kernel has now failed 5 optimization attempts; the SharedMemoryConflicts bottleneck (7.9-way bank conflicts, ~60% excessive wavefronts) appears to be structural and resistant to tile-size and load-pattern changes.
framework_notes: In Triton, when BLOCK_M is a hardcoded constexpr (not an autotune parameter), the grid must be manually updated to match. If the autotune configs do not include BLOCK_M in their Config dicts, the grid lambda using meta['BLOCK_M'] will fail or use the wrong value. The accumulator tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32) directly determines minimum register usage: BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128 requires 128×128=16384 fp32 values = 512 registers per warp = 16 registers per thread minimum just for the accumulator, before any other register usage. On Hopper (sm_90), 252 registers/thread with 256 threads/block = 64512 registers/block, exceeding the 65536 register file per SM, limiting to 1 block/SM.
